knowledge:
- key_parameters: polyLength=minimum length of poly-A/T/etc. tail to trim or handle during generic read import ;; gap=maximum distance between alignments/loci to be merged or considered part of the same segment ;; RKPM=reads per kilobase per million threshold used in heuristic segmentation of small RNAs ;; largeness=size threshold for candidate loci processing to prevent memory issues ;; prop=critical methylation proportion threshold above which a segment is considered methylated ;; FDR=False Discovery Rate threshold for filtering identified loci ;; nullData=logical indicating whether to estimate likelihoods for non-expressed/null regions during differential analysis ;; nonconversion=vector of non-conversion rates for each sample in bisulphite sequencing
- alternatives: YAMA (Yet Another Methylome Aligner) is recommended for aligning bisulphite-treated reads because it retains multi-mapping reads and reports alternate matches, which segmentSeq uses to weight methylation calls. baySeq is used internally and is the preferred package for downstream differential expression/methylation analysis.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have replicated high-throughput sequencing alignment data (small RNA-seq or bisulphite-treated DNA-seq) and want to simultaneously define consensus loci across replicates and identify differentially expressed or differentially methylated regions.
- pitfalls: High-throughput sequencing datasets are massive, so parallel processing using a cluster (cl) is highly recommended; omitting it can lead to extremely long runtimes. Results may vary slightly when using parallel processing due to non-deterministic elements in the empirical Bayesian methods. High coverage of unmethylated cytosines within a methylation locus can cause the locus to be split into fragments; use mergeMethSegs to resolve this. The replicates slot must be a factor, otherwise functions will throw warnings and convert it automatically.

workflows.name: small_rna_loci_and_de_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify small RNA loci from alignment files and perform differential expression analysis across replicate groups.
workflows.stages: 1. Read alignment files using readGeneric ;; 2. Process alignment data to find candidate loci using processAD ;; 3. Perform heuristic segmentation using heuristicSeg ;; 4. Perform empirical Bayesian segmentation using classifySeg ;; 5. Plot the segmented genome using plotGenome ;; 6. Select high-confidence loci using selectLoci ;; 7. Define experimental groups using groups ;; 8. Estimate priors using getPriors ;; 9. Estimate posterior likelihoods using getLikelihoods ;; 10. Retrieve top differentially expressed loci using topCounts
workflows.code:
datadir <- system.file("extdata", package = "segmentSeq")
libfiles <- c("SL9.txt", "SL10.txt", "SL26.txt", "SL32.txt")
libnames <- c("SL9", "SL10", "SL26", "SL32")
replicates <- c("AGO6", "AGO6", "AGO4", "AGO4")
aD <- readGeneric(files = libfiles, dir = datadir, replicates = replicates, libnames = libnames, polyLength = 10, header = TRUE, gap = 200)
sD <- processAD(aD, cl = cl)
hS <- heuristicSeg(sD = sD, aD = aD, RKPM = 1000, largeness = 1e8, getLikes = TRUE, cl = cl)
cS <- classifySeg(sD = sD, aD = aD, cD = hS, cl = cl)
par(mfrow = c(2,1), mar = c(2,6,2,2))
plotGenome(aD, hS, chr = ">Chr1", limits = c(1, 1e5), showNumber = FALSE, cap = 50)
plotGenome(aD, cS, chr = ">Chr1", limits = c(1, 1e5), showNumber = FALSE, cap = 50)
loci <- selectLoci(cS, FDR = 0.05)
groups(cS) <- list(NDE = c(1,1,1,1), DE = c("AGO6", "AGO6", "AGO4", "AGO4"))
cS <- getPriors(cS, cl = cl)
cS <- getLikelihoods(cS, nullData = TRUE, cl = cl)
topCounts(cS, NULL, number = 3)
topCounts(cS, "NDE", number = 3)
topCounts(cS, "DE", number = 3)

workflows.name: methylation_loci_and_dm_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify cytosine methylation loci from bisulphite sequencing data and perform differential methylation analysis.
workflows.stages: 1. Read methylation files using readMeths ;; 2. Plot methylation distribution using plotMethDistribution ;; 3. Process alignment data to find candidate loci using processAD ;; 4. Perform heuristic segmentation using heuristicSeg ;; 5. Merge split loci using mergeMethSegs ;; 6. Estimate posterior likelihoods on loci using lociLikelihoods ;; 7. Plot methylation loci using plotMeth ;; 8. Define experimental groups using groups ;; 9. Pre-calculate observables using methObservables ;; 10. Set density function to bbNCDist using densityFunction ;; 11. Estimate priors using getPriors ;; 12. Estimate posterior likelihoods using getLikelihoods ;; 13. Retrieve top differentially methylated regions using topCounts
workflows.code:
datadir <- system.file("extdata", package = "segmentSeq")
files <- c(
  "short_18B_C24_C24_trim.fastq_CG_methCalls.gz",
  "short_Sample_17A_trimmed.fastq_CG_methCalls.gz",
  "short_13_C24_col_trim.fastq_CG_methCalls.gz",
  "short_Sample_28_trimmed.fastq_CG_methCalls.gz")
mD <- readMeths(files = files, dir = datadir, libnames = c("A1", "A2", "B1", "B2"), replicates = c("A","A","B","B"), nonconversion = c(0.004777, 0.005903, 0.016514, 0.006134))
par(mfrow = c(2,1))
dists <- plotMethDistribution(mD, main = "Distributions of methylation", chr = "Chr1")
plotMethDistribution(mD, subtract = rowMeans(sapply(dists, function(x) x[,2])), main = "Differences between distributions", chr = "Chr1")
sD <- processAD(mD, cl = cl)
thresh = 0.2
hS <- heuristicSeg(sD = sD, aD = mD, prop = thresh, cl = cl, gap = 100, getLikes = FALSE)
hS <- mergeMethSegs(hS, mD, gap = 5000, cl = cl)
hSL <- lociLikelihoods(hS, mD, cl = cl)
plotMeth(mD, hSL, chr = "Chr1", limits = c(1, 50000), cap = 10)
groups(hSL) <- list(NDE = c(1,1,1,1), DE = c("A", "A", "B", "B"))
hSL <- methObservables(hSL)
densityFunction(hSL) <- bbNCDist
hSL <- getPriors(hSL, cl = cl)
hSL <- getLikelihoods(hSL, cl = cl)
topCounts(hSL, "DE")
